heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to EOR & PEO in Egypt
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for EOR & PEO in Egypt.

steps.title: Document Collection
steps.text: Gather essential documents from the employee, including National ID (or passport for foreigners), tax identification number, and bank account details.

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.text: Draft a compliant employment contract in Arabic (triplicate) as required by Egyptian Labor Law No. 12 of 2003. English translations are for reference only.

steps.title: Social Insurance Registration
steps.text: Register the employee with the Social Insurance Authority (Form 1) and Tax Authority immediately upon hiring to avoid penalties.

steps.title: Work Permits (Foreigners)
steps.text: For foreign nationals, the EOR manages the application for work permits and security clearances, which can take 3-6 months. Note the 10% foreign quota.

steps.title: Bank Account Setup
steps.text: Employees must have a valid local bank account (IBAN) for payroll processing. Salary transfer via Instapay or local ACH is standard.

steps.title: Notice Period
steps.text: Minimum 2 months for service under 10 years, and 3 months for service over 10 years. Notice must be written.

steps.title: Form 6 Submission
steps.text: Submit 'Form 6' to the Social Insurance Authority to de-register the employee upon exit.

steps.title: Severance Pay
steps.text: For unjustified termination, severance is typically 2 months of gross salary for each year of service.

steps.title: End of Service Bonus
steps.text: Review if the contract or internal policy mandates an 'End of Service' gratuity distinct from severance.

rows.label: Management Fee
values: Monthly flat fee per employee. Varies by volume and provider tier.

rows.label: Employer Burden
values: Includes Social Insurance (18.75%), Medical (3.25%), & other levies.

rows.label: Security Deposit
values: 1-2 Months Salary
Refundable deposit held by EOR to cover liability and notice periods.

rows.label: Work Permit Fee
values: One-time fee for processing foreign worker permits (excluding gov fees).

items.title: The 10% Quota
items.text: Foreign employees cannot exceed 10% of the total workforce in any Egyptian entity (exceptions exist for Free Zones).

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Maximum 3 months. It cannot be renewed. During probation, either party can terminate without notice/severance.

items.title: Fixed vs Indefinite
items.text: Fixed-term contracts (up to 5 years) are common. If renewed repeatedly, they may legally convert to indefinite status.

items.title: Retirement Age
items.text: The statutory retirement age is 60. Employees can continue past this age with mutual agreement, but social insurance rules change.

items.title: Deel
items.text: Strong presence in Egypt with localized support and contract templates.

items.title: Remote
items.text: Offers flat-rate pricing and owns its local entity in Egypt for better IP protection.

items.title: Papaya Global
items.text: Excellent for enterprise clients needing detailed payroll analytics and compliance reporting.

items.question: Can I hire foreign workers via EOR in Egypt?
items.answer: Yes, but strict quotas apply. Ensure the EOR partner has sufficient 'headroom' in their quota to sponsor your candidate.

items.question: Is a written contract mandatory?
items.answer: Yes, a written contract in Arabic is mandatory. If not displayed, the employee can prove rights by any means.

items.question: What is the 13th Month?
items.answer: It is not statutory but is a very common cultural expectation. Most EORs will ask if you want to include it.

items.question: How are leaves handled?
items.answer: 21 days annual leave (30 after 10 years or age 50). Sick leave requires a medical certificate and is paid.

rows.label: Provider Fee
values: $15 - $35 / employee
Monthly processing fee for local payroll bureaus. Setup fees may apply.

rows.label: Social Security (Employer)
values: Capped at EGP 14,500 monthly salary (2025 limit). Min base EGP 2,300.

rows.label: Health Insurance
values: Allocated to the Universal Health Insurance system (rolling out by governorate).

rows.label: Training Fund
values: 1% of Net Profit
Or calculated on payroll base if profit unclear. Specific to industrial/large entities.

steps.title: Salary Calculation (25th)
steps.text: Close payroll data, including overtime and variable pay. Calculate gross-to-net and social insurance.

steps.title: Disbursement (28th-30th)
steps.text: Transfer net salaries to employee bank accounts. Use local ACH or bank letters for bulk transfers.

steps.title: payslip Issuance (30th)
steps.text: Issue detailed payslips in Arabic (mandatory) or bilingual. Must show all deductions clearly.

steps.title: Tax Remittance (15th Next Month)
steps.text: Deadline to pay withheld income tax and social insurance contributions to their respective authorities.

items.title: Mandatory EGP Payment
items.text: Local employees MUST be paid in Egyptian Pounds (EGP) within Egypt. Paying in USD is generally restricted for local contracts.

items.title: Instapay & Wallets
items.text: Digital wallets (Vodafone Cash) and Instapay are valid disbursement methods for smaller amounts or unbanked staff.

items.title: Expense Reimbursement
items.text: Reimbursed expenses are non-taxable if supported by original VAT invoices. Flat allowances are fully taxable.

items.title: Local Compliance
items.text: Ensure your software supports Egyptian tax brackets (updated annually) and generates Form 4-Salary.

items.title: Major Players
items.text: SAP SuccessFactors and Oracle are dominant in enterprise. Odoo and MenaHR are popular for mid-market.

items.title: E-Invoicing
items.text: Payroll systems often need to integrate with the ETA's e-invoicing portal for certain contractor payments.

items.question: Can I pay bonuses in USD?
items.answer: Technically, local payments should be EGP. Some companies pay USD into USD accounts, but this carries regulatory risk.

items.question: Are meal allowances taxable?
items.answer: In-kind meals (cafeteria) are exempt. Cash meal allowances are taxable salary.

items.question: What is the penalty for late tax payment?
items.answer: A delay fee calculated at the Central Bank discount rate plus 2% is applied.

rows.label: Social Insurance (Total)
values: Combined Employer (18.75%) and Employee (11%) contribution. Covers pension, disability, and death.

rows.label: Universal Health Ins.
values: Varies by family status. Employer pays part, employee pays part. Rolling out gradually across governorates.

rows.label: Emergency Fund
values: Based on basic salary, paid by the employer to the Ministry of Manpower.

items.title: Annual Leave
items.text: 21 days per year (standard). increases to 30 days after 10 years of service or upon reaching age 50.

items.title: Sick Leave
items.text: Up to 180 days. 75% - 85% of wage paid by Social Insurance Authority, not the employer (though employers often top it up).

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.text: 90 days required by law for the first 3 children (fully paid). Paternity leave is not statutory but becoming common.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.text: Typically 15-20 days per year. The Prime Minister announces specific dates annually.

items.title: Private Medical Insurance
items.text: Almost mandatory for attracting white-collar talent. Top providers: AXA, Allianz, MetLife, Bupa.

items.title: Transportation
items.text: Providing buses or a cash allowance is standard due to Cairo's traffic conditions.

items.title: Ramadan Bonus
items.text: Many local companies provide a bonus (box of food or cash) during the holy month of Ramadan.

items.title: Can unused leave be cashed out?
items.text: Yes, upon termination, accrued but unused annual leave must be paid out based on gross salary.

items.title: Is profit sharing mandatory?
items.text: Yes, for LLCs and JSCs, 10% of distributable net profits must be allocated to employees (capped at 12 months' salary).

rows.label: Social Insurance Share
values: Based on EGP 14,500 Salary Cap

rows.label: Emergency Fund
values: On Base Salary (Max limits may apply)

rows.label: Martyrs Fund
values: On Gross Salary
Up to 3,333

steps.title: Determine Social Insurance Salary
steps.description: Identify the 'Social Insurance Salary' amount, capped at EGP 14,500/month (2025). Calculate 11% (employee) and 18.75% (employer).

steps.title: Deduct Social Insurance
steps.description: Subtract the 11% employee contribution from the total gross salary to get the Tax Base.

steps.title: Apply Exemption
steps.description: Deduct the personal allowance (EGP 20,000/year or ~EGP 1,666/month) from the Tax Base.

steps.title: Calculate Tax
steps.description: Apply the progressive tax brackets (10% to 27.5%) to the remaining amount.

steps.title: Final Deductions
steps.description: Subtract the calculated tax and 1% Martyrs fund/Emergency fund from the Gross to arrive at Net Pay.

faqs.question: What is the 2025 personal exemption?
faqs.answer: The personal tax exemption is EGP 20,000 per year.

faqs.question: Does the employer pay 'Martyrs Fund'?
faqs.answer: The Martyrs Fund (0.0005%) is typically deducted from the employee's gross, though some employers cover it as a benefit.

faqs.question: Are meal allowances taxable?
faqs.answer: Meal allowances provided in-kind (e.g., cafeteria) are often exempt, but cash allowances are fully taxable as salary.

items.title: Net Salary
items.text: Gross - (Social Insurance + Income Tax).

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: Customary in MNCs but not legally required.

items.title: Profit Share
items.text: 10% of distributable profits for LLCs/JSCs.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Egypt
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Egypt.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.text: Submit at least 3 proposed company names to the Commercial Registry to obtain a non-confusion certificate.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening
steps.text: Open a 'company under formation' bank account and deposit the minimum capital (if required) to obtain a bank certificate.

steps.title: Document Submission
steps.text: Submit Articles of Association, power of attorney, and bank certificate to GAFI (General Authority for Investment).

steps.title: Notarization & Registration
steps.text: Notarize the Articles of Association and register with the Commercial Registry and Tax Authority.

rows.label: Government Fees
values: Includes notary fees, chamber certification, and gazette publication fees (capital dependent).

rows.label: Legal Fees
values: Professional fees for lawyers to draft documents and handle GAFI procedures.

rows.label: Minimum Capital (LLC)
values: Nominal
No strict minimum for LLCs, but typically EGP 10,000 - 50,000 is recommended for credibility.

items.title: LLC (Limited Liability Company)
items.text: Most common for foreign investors. Liability limited to shares. Can be 100% foreign-owned in many sectors.

items.title: Branch Office
items.text: Only for executing a specific contract in Egypt. Requires a manager (can be foreign) and follows parent company activities.

items.title: Security Clearance
items.text: Foreign shareholders often undergo a security check, which can delay the process by several months.

items.title: Power of Attorney
items.text: Legalized POA from foreign parent company to local counsel.

items.title: Parent Company Docs
items.text: Certificate of incorporation and articles of association of the parent company (legalized/apostilled).

items.title: Lease Agreement
items.text: Signed lease for a physical office space in Egypt (virtual offices are often restricted for initial setup).

items.question: Is there a minimum capital?
items.answer: No strict minimum for LLCs, but EGP 10k-50k is recommended.

items.question: Can a foreigner be a director?
items.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership and management is allowed for LLCs.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Typically 2-4 weeks if documents are legalized.

heroData.title: Staffing in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Egypt
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Egypt.

rows.label: Contingency Recruiting
values: Percentage of first-year gross salary. Paid only upon successful placement.

rows.label: Executive Search
values: Retained search for C-level roles. 1/3 upfront, 1/3 shortlist, 1/3 placement.

rows.label: RPO (High Volume)
values: Fixed Monthly + Success Fee
Recruitment Process Outsourcing for scaling teams (e.g., call centers).

rows.label: Contract Staffing
values: 15% - 25% Markup
Monthly markup on contractor's salary covering payroll admin and margin.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.text: Agencies source candidates through local networks, LinkedIn, and job boards like Wuzzuf and Bayt.

steps.title: Screening
steps.text: Initial screening interviews and skills assessments are conducted by the agency. English proficiency checks are standard.

steps.title: Interviewing
steps.text: Client interviews (virtual or in-person). Technical assessments (HackerRank) are common for tech roles.

steps.title: Placement & Offer
steps.text: Upon selection, the agency assists with salary negotiation and offer letters (bilingual recommended).

steps.title: Guarantee Period
steps.text: Standard guarantee period is typically 3 months, offering a free replacement if the hire leaves.

items.title: Tech Hubs
items.text: Cairo (Maadi, Smart Village) is the primary hub. Alexandria and Assiut are emerging with strong university talent pools.

items.title: Language Skills
items.text: Egypt produces 500k+ graduates annually. High proficiency in English, French, and German for BPO sectors.

items.title: Salary Inflation
items.text: Tech salaries are rising fast due to remote work competition. Senior devs can command $2k-$4k/month.

items.title: Labor Law 2025
items.text: New provisions in Law No. 14 simplify termination for poor performance, encouraging more direct hiring.

items.title: Wuzzuf
items.text: The leading tech and white-collar job board in Egypt.

items.title: Bayt
items.text: Regional giant covering the entire MENA region.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.text: Essential for mid-to-senior level professional roles.

items.question: What is the average time to hire?
items.answer: 4-6 weeks for mid-level roles; 2-3 months for executive positions.

items.question: Are background checks legal?
items.answer: Yes, but they require candidate consent. Criminal record checks ('Fish wa Tashbih') are standard.

items.question: Can I hire contractors indefinitely?
items.answer: Careful structuring is needed to avoid 'deemed employee' risks after prolonged engagement.

steps.title: Phase 1: Ministry Approval
steps.text: Submit application to the Ministry of Manpower. Requires proof that no qualified local is available (although often waived for experts).

steps.title: Phase 2: Security Clearance
steps.text: The National Security Agency conducts a background check. This is the longest phase, taking 2-6 months depending on nationality.

steps.title: Phase 3: HIV Test
steps.text: The applicant must undergo an HIV test at a specific government Ministry of Health laboratory in Egypt.

steps.title: Phase 4: Permit Issuance
steps.text: Once cleared, the work permit is issued (valid for 1 year, renewable). Residency visa is stamped in the passport.

rows.label: Government Fee (Initial)
values: Varies by year. Fees for first-time issuance are higher than renewals. Paid in EGP (some exemptions require USD).

rows.label: Legal/Agency Fees
values: Professional fees for handling the complex paperwork and ministry follow-ups.

rows.label: Medical Test
values: Cost for the mandatory HIV and health screening.

items.title: 10% Foreign Quota
items.text: Strictly enforced. For every 1 foreigner, you generally need 9 registered Egyptian employees on social insurance.

items.title: Reciprocity Principle
items.text: Egypt applies reciprocity; fees and ease of obtaining permits often depend on the applicant's home country policies towards Egyptians.

items.title: Dependents
items.text: Dependent visas for family do NOT grant the right to work. A separate work permit is required for a spouse to work.

items.title: Can I work on a tourist visa?
items.text: No. Working on a tourist visa is illegal and can lead to deportation and fines for the employer.

items.title: How long does renewal take?
items.text: Renewal is faster than initial issuance, typically 1-2 months. Must start process before expiry.

items.title: Is there a Golden Visa?
items.text: Yes, long-term residency (5-10 years) is available for property owners or large deposits ($50k - $100k) in local banks.

items.title: Global Agencies
items.text: Fragomen and Santa Fe Relocation have offices or strong partners in Cairo.

items.title: Local Law Firms
items.text: Top firms like Matouk Bassiouny, Zulficar & Partners, and Sharkawy & Sarhan handle complex corporate immigration.

heroData.title: HRIS in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Egypt
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for HRIS in Egypt.

items.title: ZenHR
items.text: Leading regional provider with full localization for Egypt taxes and social insurance.

items.title: Menaitech
items.text: Comprehensive suite widely used in the MENA region, offering strong compliance features.

items.title: Mozon
items.text: Designed specifically for the Egyptian market, integrating biometric attendance and payroll.

items.title: Zoho Payroll
items.text: Offers a localized edition for Egypt, popular among SMEs for its ease of use.

items.title: Social Insurance Forms
items.text: System must generate 'Form 1' (hiring), 'Form 6' (exit), and monthly social insurance reports.

items.title: New Labor Provisions
items.text: Must handle new leave types under Law 2025 (e.g., paternity leave, extended maternity leave).

items.title: Arabic Support
items.text: Generate contracts and payslips in Arabic as required by law.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.text: Migrate employee data, ensuring all statutory fields (National ID, Social Insurance No) are captured.

steps.title: Policy Configuration
steps.text: Configure leave policies, overtime rules (+35%/+70%), and tax brackets.

steps.title: Integration
steps.text: Integrate with biometric attendance devices and general ledger systems.

items.question: Is cloud HRIS accepted?
items.answer: Yes, cloud solutions are widely adopted, provided they comply with data privacy laws.

items.question: Must data be hosted locally?
items.answer: While preferred for sensitive data, many global providers serve Egypt compliant with cross-border transfer rules.

items.question: Can it handle tax tiers?
items.answer: Yes, a localized HRIS automatically updates tax tiers which change frequently in Egypt.

items.title: Localization
items.text: Ensure the system supports Arabic right-to-left UI and local tax rules.

items.title: Data Residency
items.text: PDPL allows cloud hosting if security standards are met.

items.title: Mobile & Whatsapp
items.text: High mobile penetration makes WhatsApp-integrated HR tools popular.

heroData.title: Accounting in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Accounting in Egypt
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Accounting in Egypt.

steps.title: Auditor Appointment
steps.text: All LLCs and JSCs must appoint an external auditor listed on the Ministry of Finance registry. Appointment is ratified at the AGM.

steps.title: E-Invoicing Registration
steps.text: Mandatory for all companies. Integration with the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) portal is required for VAT deduction.

steps.title: Books Preparation
steps.text: Prepare Journal, Ledger, and Inventory books. Must be in Arabic and available for inspection.

steps.title: Financial Statement Submission
steps.text: Submit audited financials to GAFI and the Tax Authority within 4 months of year-end (usually by April 30).

rows.label: Annual Audit Fee
values: For SMEs. Big 4 firms charge significantly higher ($10k+).

rows.label: Monthly Bookkeeping
values: Outsourced service including VAT filing and basic reporting.

rows.label: Electronic Signature
values: EGP 2,000 / year
Required for e-Invoicing and digital tax portals (Token fees).

rows.label: Tax Consultation
values: Advisory for complex transfer pricing or cross-border tax issues.

items.title: EAS Standards
items.text: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) are mandatory. They closely mirror IFRS with minor local variations.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: Standard FY is Jan 1 - Dec 31. Changing it requires ETA approval.

items.title: Digital Records
items.text: Digital record-keeping is now recognized and preferred, but original paper invoices may still be requested during audits.

items.title: April 30
items.text: Deadline for Corporate Income Tax return (Form 27) and Financial Statements.

items.title: Monthly (VAT)
items.text: VAT returns (Form 10) must be filed by the last day of the month following the reporting period.

items.title: Quarterly (Salary Tax)
items.text: Form 4-Salary is due in Jan, Apr, July, Oct.

items.title: E-Invoicing
items.text: Mandatory for all VAT-registered entities in Egypt.

items.title: Arabic Ledger
items.text: Official journals must be kept in Arabic.

items.title: Retention
items.text: Records must be preserved for 5 years for tax audit purposes.

steps.title: Form 1 (Hiring)
steps.text: Must be submitted to Social Insurance office within 2 weeks of hiring to register an employee.

steps.title: Form 6 (Exit)
steps.text: Submitted upon termination or resignation. Employee signature is often required to avoid disputes.

steps.title: Form 2 (Establishment)
steps.text: Biannual submission detailing the entire workforce structure, salaries, and emergency contacts.

steps.title: Labor Office Audits
steps.text: Inspectors randomly check for safety rights, child labor violations, and contract copies.

rows.label: Late Tax Filing
values: 3% - 20% + Interest
Percentage of unpaid tax. Interest is typically 2% above assessments.

rows.label: Social Insurance Evasion
values: EGP 20k - 100k
Prison time possible for repeated offenses or falsifying salary data.

rows.label: Data Privacy Breach (PDPL)
values: Up to EGP 5M
Fines under new PDPL for mishandling personal data without consent.

items.title: Law No. 151 of 2020
items.text: Egypt's version of GDPR. Protects 'personal data' and requires user consent for processing.

items.title: Cross-Border Transfer
items.text: Transferring data outside Egypt requires a license unless the recipient country has adequate protection (standard is high).

items.title: DPO Requirement
items.text: Companies processing sensitive data must appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) registered with the Center.

items.title: Work Rules Regulation
items.text: Companies with 10+ employees must post internal work regulations (approved by Labor Office).

items.title: Health & Safety
items.text: Mandatory committee for companies with >50 employees to oversee workplace safety.

items.title: Whistleblowing
items.text: Not legislated strictly but recommended for multinational subsidiaries to align with global FCPA/UK Bribery Act.

items.question: Can I use electronic signatures?
items.answer: Yes, e-Signatures are legally binding if issued by a licensed certification authority (e.g., Egypt Trust).

items.question: Are strikes legal?
items.answer: Yes, but they are strictly regulated and must be approved by the relevant trade union committee.

items.question: Must contracts be in Arabic?
items.answer: Yes. A bilingual contract is fine, but the Arabic text prevails in court.

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
values: Standard rate on net taxable profits. 40.55% for oil & gas.

rows.label: Value Added Tax (VAT)
values: Standard rate. Machinery/Equipment is 5%. Exports are 0%.

rows.label: Dividend WHT
values: 5% if listed on EGX; 10% if unlisted. May be reduced by DTT.

rows.label: Service WHT
values: Withholding on payments to non-residents for services/royalties.

steps.title: Tax Card Issuance
steps.text: Obtained during incorporation (now integrated). Valid for 5 years.

steps.title: VAT Registration
steps.text: Mandatory if annual revenue > EGP 500,000. Voluntary registration possible below threshold.

steps.title: E-Token Setup
steps.text: Purchase an e-Invoicing token (eSeal or eSignature) to authorize filings on the portal.

items.title: Strategic Investment Projects
items.text: Deduction of 30-50% of investment costs from taxable profits for up to 7 years (Investment Law).

items.title: Public Free Zones
items.text: Exempt from Corporate Tax. Subject to 1% duty on value added (projects not allowed to sell into local market without customs).

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: Egypt has treaty networks with 60+ countries (UAE, UK, US, Germany) to prevent double taxation.

items.question: What is the statute of limitations?
items.answer: Generally 5 years for tax audits. Can be extended in cases of evasion.

items.question: Is Transfer Pricing applicable?
items.answer: Yes. Companies with related party transactions must file a Master File and Local File annually.

items.question: Can I claim VAT refunds?
items.answer: Yes, for capital goods (machines) or if in a credit position for 6 consecutive periods.

items.title: Tax Year
items.text: Follows the calendar year: Jan 1 - Dec 31.

items.title: Currency
items.text: Taxes are payable in EGP.

items.title: Registration Threshold
items.text: EGP 500,000 annual turnover for VAT.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to MSA & Legal in Egypt
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for MSA & Legal in Egypt.

rows.label: Contract Review
values: Rate for bilingual senior associates at top-tier Cairo firms.

rows.label: CRCICA Arbitration Fee
values: $3,000 + Admin Fees
Filing fee for arbitration at the Cairo Regional Centre. Total costs depend on dispute value.

rows.label: Legal Translation
values: Certified translation required for court submission.

rows.label: Notarization
values: 0.5% of Value
Notary public fees for certain deeds, capped at EGP 100,000 typically.

steps.title: Scope of Work (SOW)
steps.text: Clearly define deliverables and timelines. Ambiguity in SOW is the #1 cause of disputes in Egyptian service contracts.

steps.title: Payment Terms & Currency
steps.text: Specify if payment is in USD or EGP. Local entities dealing with local entities must transact in EGP by law.

steps.title: Confidentiality (NDA)
steps.text: Include robust confidentiality clauses. Reference the new Data Protection Law (PDPL) for personal data handling.

steps.title: Termination Clause
steps.text: Define notice periods (e.g., 30-60 days). 'Termination for convenience' is valid but must be explicitly stated.

items.title: Software Registration
items.text: Source code can be registered with ITIDA (Information Technology Industry Development Agency) to prove ownership.

items.title: Work-for-Hire
items.text: Egyptian law defaults to the creator owning IP unless explicitly assigned in writing to the employer/client.

items.title: Trademarks
items.text: Registered with the Internal Trade Development Authority. Process takes 12-18 months.

items.title: Arbitration Preference
items.text: Arbitration (CRCICA) is strongly preferred over local courts due to speed (1-2 years vs 5-10 years).

items.title: Governing Law
items.text: Egyptian Civil Law typically governs. Foreign law can be chosen for international contracts but public order rules still apply.

items.title: Language Priority
items.text: Even if the contract is in English, the Arabic translation will supersede in local courts.

items.question: Is arbitration enforceable?
items.answer: Yes, Egypt is a signatory to the New York Convention. Arbitral awards are generally enforced without reviewing merits.

items.question: Can I use foreign law?
items.answer: Yes, for international contracts (e.g., between a US company and an Egyptian vendor), but mandatory local labor/crimanal laws apply.

items.question: Are digital signatures valid?
items.answer: Yes, under the E-Signature Law No. 15 of 2004. However, they must be issued by a licensed authority to be self-proving in court.

items.question: What is the statute of limitations?
items.answer: 15 years for general civil claims, but shorter for commercial obligations (7 years) and labor claims (1 year).

heroData.title: Software Solutions in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Access the Middle East's Leading Tech Hub
heroData.description: Navigate Egypt's booming tech ecosystem, from outsourcing hubs in Smart Village to competitive dev rates offering high ROI.

items.title: Smart Village (Cairo)
items.text: Located on the outskirts of Cairo, this is the premier technology park hosting multinationals like Microsoft, IBM, and Vodafone. It offers world-class infrastructure and reliable connectivity.

items.title: Maadi Technology Park
items.text: A key outsourcing hub with high-speed fiber infrastructure, heavily favored by BPO and contact center operators due to its accessibility and density of talent.

items.title: Alexandria
items.text: Egypt's second capital offers a growing pool of talent from Alexandria University, often at slightly lower rates than Cairo, with a strong focus on maritime and logistics tech.

rows.label: Junior Developer
values: 1-3 years experience. Strong foundational skills but may need oversight. Annual salary approx $10k - $15k.

rows.label: Senior Engineer
values: 5+ years experience. Capable of architectural decisions and team leadership. Annual salary approx $35k - $55k.

rows.label: Outsourcing Agency Rate
values: Standard blended rate for a dedicated team from a mid-tier Egyptian agency. Includes PM and QA support.

rows.label: Mobile App MVP
values: Fixed cost for a standard cross-platform MVP (Flutter/React Native) delivered in 3-4 months.

steps.title: Define Scope & Stack
steps.description: Egypt has strong talent in PHP (Laravel), .NET, and increasingly Python and JS frameworks. Define your stack early to target the right agencies.

steps.title: Verify Portfolio
steps.description: Check for experience with Western clients (US/UK/EU) to ensure communication alignment and time zone overlap handling.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Conduct code reviews or pilot projects. HackerRank scores for Egyptian devs are typically high in problem-solving.

steps.title: Contracting
steps.description: Ensure the contract specifies IP transfer upon payment. Egyptian law protects creator rights by default unless assigned.

items.title: Payment Gateways
items.description: Fawry and Paymob are market leaders. Integration with these is crucial for local e-commerce success.

items.title: Internet Connectivity
items.description: While improving, stability can vary in residential areas. Ensure your remote team has backup 4G/5G connections (Vodafone/Etisalat are top providers).

items.title: Time Zone
items.description: Egypt is GMT+2 (Standard) or GMT+3 (DST), offering good overlap with Europe and acceptable overlap with US East Coast mornings.

items.title: Hardware Imports
items.description: Importing custom hardware (servers, prototypes) can be bureaucratically complex. Use local procurement where possible.

faqs.question: How is English proficiency?
faqs.answer: High among tech professionals. Most university technical education is conducted in English, and many devs speak fluent business English.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives for tech?
faqs.answer: Yes, companies in technology parks (like Maadi) often enjoy tax exemptions and simplified customs for hardware.

faqs.question: What is the turnover rate?
faqs.answer: Turnover can be high (15-20%) as skilled devs are poached by European firms offering remote work. Retention bonuses and clear career paths are recommended.

heroData.title: Marketing in Egypt
heroData.subtitle: Dominate the Largest Arabic-Speaking Market
heroData.description: From high-impact billboards on the Ring Road to viral TikTok campaigns, navigate Egypt's diverse media landscape.

items.title: WhatsApp Commerce
items.text: WhatsApp is not just for chat; it's a primary sales channel for SMEs and retail. Automated bots and catalog integration are essential for conversion.

items.title: Short-Form Video
items.text: TikTok and Instagram Reels consumption is exploding. Content must be localized to 'Egyptian Arabic' humor and trends to go viral.

items.title: Cash on Delivery (COD)
items.text: Despite fintech growth, a large segment of consumers still prefers COD. Marketing funnels must account for this confirmation step to reduce returns.

rows.label: Monthly Retainer (Full Service)
values: Covers strategy, social media management, & partial content creation. High-end boutique agencies may charge more.

rows.label: SEO Services
values: Monthly fee for technical SEO, content optimization, and backlinking. Price varies by keyword difficulty.

rows.label: Billboard (Cairo Prime)
values: Monthly rental for static sites in high-traffic areas like Mohandessin, Zamalek, or the Ring Road.

rows.label: LED Screen (Prime)
values: High-impact digital OOH locations with heavy traffic visibility. Often sold in rotation slots.

steps.title: Cultural Localization
steps.description: Translate assets into Egyptian Colloquial Arabic (Masri). Standard Arabic (Fusha) can feel distant for B2C brands.

steps.title: Influencer Selection
steps.description: Engage micro-influencers (10k-50k followers) for higher engagement. Verify their audience demographics to avoid 'bot' followers.

steps.title: Platform Setup
steps.description: Set up Facebook Business Manager with local payment methods if possible to avoid currency blocking issues.

steps.title: Launch & A/B Testing
steps.description: Test creatives intensely in the first week. Egyptian audiences react quickly to trends, so agility is key.

items.title: Medical Ads
items.description: Strict new 2025 regulations require prior Ministry of Health approval for any ad related to health services or products.

items.title: Influencer Taxes
items.description: Influencers are now required to register for VAT and income tax. Ensure your contracts reflect tax liability and invoicing requirements.

items.title: Contests & Giveaways
items.description: Promotional contests require notification and permits from the Consumer Protection Agency to ensure fairness.

faqs.question: Is TV still relevant?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially during Ramadan. TV ad rates skyrocket during this month, capturing massive family viewership for major brand campaigns.

faqs.question: Which social platform is #1?
faqs.answer: Facebook remains the absolute giant in terms of reach (50m+ users), but TikTok is winning the 'time spent' metric among youth (under 25s).

faqs.question: Can I target by wealth?
faqs.answer: Indirectly. Targeting by device type (latest iPhone) and specific geographies (e.g., New Cairo, Sheikh Zayed, El Gouna) is a common proxy.
